title: Your K-pop Position

intake.question: In a group project, you're usually...

options.label: The one who keeps it fun
The one quietly doing the hard part
The one who presents it and shines

intake.question: If you had to be famous for one thing?

plan.title: Your position in the group (it's obvious)
Group drama, and what you do
Your solo era, planned by Yeon

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. You'd take the {pos_lower} spot and three others if the company let you.

Bom: You carry the group on bad days.

Yeon: You also correct the choreo in the group chat at 1am. Members have muted you. Lovingly.

Your growth arc: let someone else lead one stage this comeback. Watch what you learn from the side.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd lead the group, the fandom and the catering if allowed.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You shine best inside the group, holding it together from the middle.

Yeon: Which is why you never ask for more lines. And then quietly sulk about the line distribution.

Bom: You're allowed to want a solo moment.

Ask for one thing this era: a line, a spot, a part. Out loud. Producers can't read minds either.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for the line. You've earned the line.

strong.text:
On stage, a strong chart looks like certainty. Big expressions, clean hits, eye contact that reaches row Z.

Yeon: And when the camera does land on you, you keep it. Ending fairy, ten full seconds, camera held hostage.

Bom: Hand it off once in a while. Generosity on stage reads as confidence too.

Watch one stage back with the sound off. Most of the time the space you take is exactly right. Sometimes a member is standing in your shadow, and half a step sideways fixes it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You hold the camera like it owes you rent. Share it.

weak.text:
Light chart on stage: all feeling. Warm room, close members, and you're untouchable. Cold crowd, and you wobble.

Bom: Build a tiny ritual before every stage. A word with your favourite member. One deep breath. A look at the people who came for you.

Yeon: And rehearse your entrance more than the middle. Your nerves calm down after the first eight counts.

Make those eight counts so familiar your body could do them half asleep. The rest of the song follows.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Find your people in the crowd first. Then sing to them.

strong.text:
Strong charts run the dorm whether or not anyone put them in charge.

Yeon: Opinions on the dishes, the thermostat and who gets the good shower slot. Eleven house rules. Numbered.

Bom: You also make the place feel safe. People sleep better knowing someone has things handled.

Yeon: Keep two rules. Drop nine. And knock before you handle someone else's room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two house rules, not eleven. Choose like your peace depends on it.

weak.text:
Light charts become the quiet caretaker. You notice the empty fridge and the member who skipped dinner.

Bom: Lovely. Make sure someone does it for you too.

Yeon: Say "I need a quiet night" before you need it. Nobody in that dorm is a mind reader. They can barely find their own socks.

Keep one shelf, one drawer, one hour that's only yours. In shared spaces you dissolve into everyone else's routine unless something stays yours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You feed everyone. Let someone feed you for once.

strong.text:
When a strong chart fights, the fight gets bigger. You're rarely wrong. You can be right far too loudly.

Bom: The fastest way back: a small, specific apology that doesn't argue with itself.

Yeon: No "but". The "but" eats the apology. Then snacks. Every group in history has made up over 1am convenience store snacks.

Check in the next morning. You move on fast and assume everyone else did too. A quick "we good?" finishes the repair.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Apologise without a "but". Then bring the snacks.

weak.text:
When a light chart fights, you go quiet and hope it passes. Sometimes it does.

Yeon: More often, the other member reads your silence as fury. Now there are two fights.

Bom: Say one honest sentence early, even a clumsy one. "That hurt a bit" fixes more than three days of polite distance.

If speaking feels impossible, type it. "Can we talk later, something bothered me" counts as speaking up, and it buys time to find the words.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Clumsy and honest beats three days of polite and silent.

strong.text:
Strong charts go solo with a clear vision and almost no doubt.

Yeon: Risk: a concept so polished it forgets to be a person.

Bom: Put one song on the album that scares you a little. Fans can always tell which track is really you.

Invite one member onto a track, too. Fans love old chemistry showing up in a new era, and it keeps you humble, which keeps you likeable.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One track that scares you. That's the one they'll keep.

weak.text:
Light charts go solo slowly, after someone believes in them out loud.

Bom: Let them. A small trusted team and a concept from your own life beats a big loud launch.

Yeon: You don't have to be loud alone. You have to sound like yourself.

Start small. A cover, a self-written B-side, a song for the fans. Every small release builds the nerve the big one needs.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Quiet solo eras win too. Sound like you.

peer_strong.text:
You'd count everyone's lines. Including your own. Especially your own.

Your chart is stacked with {dm_el}, your own element. Saju calls that the peer family: siblings, friends, rivals.

Yeon: Same lines, same screen time, same respect as everyone else, or there will be a conversation.

Bom: That fairness instinct is also why you're the first to defend a member who got shortchanged.

Yeon: Practice turns into a quiet contest, though. The group wins together. Write it on your water bottle.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your own element, everywhere. You'd count the lines. You'd also fight for them.

output_strong.text:
The ad-lib nobody rehearsed? Yours. The face that became a meme? Also yours.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. Saju calls it output: expression, talent, play.

Bom: Ideas spill out of you. Little moves that weren't in the choreo, faces, runs.

Yeon: Directors love it. Managers sigh into their clipboards.

Bom: Keep the spark. Learn the formation first. Freedom looks best on a clean base.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: All that {heavy_el} makes you the ad-lib monarch. Formation first, then play.

wealth_strong.text:
You'd already picked the title track. Before the A&R meeting.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. Saju calls it wealth: goals, results, what you build.

Bom: You think about the group like a project. Which concept sells. Which outfit photographs best.

Yeon: Leader-producer hybrid. Also, slightly, a spreadsheet with legs.

Bom: Members aren't schedule items. Ask how they slept before you ask if they practised.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You'd plan the whole comeback. Ask how they're doing first.

power_strong.text:
You have never missed a cue. You expect nobody else to either.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. Saju calls it power: rules, standards, discipline.

Bom: On a strong chart that reads as professionalism. Groups need someone like you.

Yeon: They also need you to laugh when a live stage goes sideways.

Bom: Mistakes on live shows are half of what fans love. Let them be funny.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Zero missed cues. Laugh when somebody else misses one.

resource_strong.text:
You've watched every stage ever filmed. Some of them twice, with notes.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. Saju calls it resource: learning, comfort, inner life.

Bom: Best interview answers in the group. You read every lyric twice before you sing it.

Yeon: You also get stuck in your head. Thinking about the move instead of doing the move.

Bom: Do it before you've finished thinking about it. Rehearsal is where thoughts become moves.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You studied every stage. Now go make one.

output_weak.text:
You give everything on stage. Then you sit silent in the van, staring out the window.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces: giving, expressing, performing.

Bom: The talent is real. So is the drain.

Yeon: You treat recovery like an optional extra. It is the main schedule item.

Bom: One full day off after a big week isn't lazy. It's how you stay good.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Guard the day after a big stage like it's a contract clause.

wealth_weak.text:
You're running the group's logistics on 4 percent battery. Again.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. Old saju books call it wealth heavy, self light: lots to manage, little backup.

Bom: Other people's moods, the comeback plan, the snack order. All you.

Yeon: The group has other members for a reason. Some of them are bored.

Bom: Delegate one thing today. Something small, so it actually happens.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Hand one task to a bored member. They'll love it.

power_weak.text:
One note from the trainer and you replay it for three days.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}: pressure, judgment, rules.

Bom: Every correction lands like a verdict. You replay bad stages in the shower.

Yeon: You're more talented than your inner critic allows. Your inner critic is a hater with no credentials.

Bom: Keep one clip of a stage you nailed. Watch it when the voice gets loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The critic in your head has never performed once. Ignore the reviews.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Bom: On stage this looks like someone completely sure of themselves who still checks the monitor after every song.

Yeon: "Was that okay?" Every song. You know it was okay.

Both are true. The plenty is visible. The root underneath is thinner. Keep members who cheer for you out loud, and believe them when they do.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sure of yourself on camera, unsure at the monitor. Both count.

output_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the output element: expression.

Yeon: Strong chart, nothing leaking out. Fans may call you cold before they figure out you're shy on camera.

Bom: Borrow some. One silly face per stage. One honest line per interview.

Yeon: And what happens when the cameras go off? That's the dorm. Next page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One silly face per stage. Proof you're human.

wealth_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the wealth element: chasing results.

Bom: You perform for the joy of it. Lovely.

Yeon: And you never ask for the part you want. Groups give lines to the people who ask.

Bom: Ask. Then turn the page. It's 1am in the dorm and someone's knocking.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Want the high note? Ask. The practice room has no mind readers.

power_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the power element: structure.

Yeon: You improvise beautifully and forget the formation. Every time.

Bom: Borrow some discipline. One extra run of the hard section each practice.

Yeon: Boring. Effective. Next page is the dorm at 1am, and I have notes about your room.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Repeat the hard eight counts. Boring works.

resource_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the resource element: being looked after.

Bom: You're strong and you almost never let anyone take care of you.

Yeon: The members bring food after a bad day and you say "I'm not hungry". You are hungry.

Bom: Eat it. Being cared for is part of being in a group. Speaking of which: the dorm, next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Accept the snack. Strong people get fed too.

output_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the output element: expression.

Bom: It keeps a light chart from burning out on stage. Good.

Yeon: It also makes you hard to read. Fans squint at you like a cryptic crossword.

Bom: Show small things. A wave to the back row. A real laugh. Then come see who you are off duty, next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiny gestures land hardest. Fans notice the small ones first.

wealth_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the wealth element: chasing.

Bom: You don't fight for the center. It keeps the peace.

Yeon: It also means people forget to offer it to you.

Bom: Ask for one moment per comeback. A line, a pose, a part. And next page, the version of you only roommates get.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One line, one pose, one part. Ask out loud.

power_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the power element: outside pressure.

Bom: Fewer rules weighing on you. That's genuinely nice.

Yeon: It also means nobody builds your routine for you. Your bedtime is currently "eventually".

Bom: A fixed warm-up and a fixed bedtime do a lot. Next page, we check what you actually do at 1am.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same warm-up, same order, every day. Your body loves a script.

resource_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the resource element: comfort and support.

Yeon: You're running on willpower and iced coffee.

Bom: Build your support on purpose. One member you can call. One place that calms you. One song that resets your head.

Yeon: Next page: the dorm. Where your reset kit either exists or doesn't.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One person, one place, one song. That's the reset kit.

none_strong.text:
All five elements turn up in your pillars. On a strong chart that's range.

Bom: You can sing the ballad, survive the dance break and still be funny on variety.

Yeon: The trap: doing everything at seventy percent. Range is not a personality.

Bom: Pick the one thing you want to be known for and push it to a hundred. Next page, the dorm, where nobody's watching.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can do everything. Pick one thing and be scary good at it.

none_weak.text:
All five elements turn up in your pillars. On a light chart that's flexibility.

Bom: Any unit, any concept, any song. You fit.

Yeon: Flexible is great. Invisible isn't. Fans can't find you in the group photo.

Bom: Keep one signature, a move, a laugh, a habit, that someone in the last row can spot. Then turn the page: off duty, 1am.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Flexible is great. Keep a signature so they can find you.

resource.title: What refills you between stages: {helper_el} (book it in)
resource.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. For your light {dm_el} chart it's {helper_el}, the element that feeds you.

Bom: In group life that means mentors, rest, actual downtime with your phone in another room.

Yeon: You're at your best after someone looks after you. So stop waiting until you crash to allow it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Running on empty helps nobody. Your refill is {helper_el}.

peer.title: What keeps you steady on tour: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. Yours already has plenty of nourishment on paper, so what steadies you is your own element, {helper_el}.

Bom: In group life that's the members themselves. A best friend in the group. A sub-unit. Someone your age to laugh with at 3am.

Yeon: Peers are your medicine. Fewer mentors, more co-conspirators.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your fix is {helper_el}: a partner in crime inside the group.

output.title: Where your extra drive should go: {helper_el}
output.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and yours is {helper_el}, the element you produce.

Bom: In group life that means making things. Writing a verse. Choreographing a bridge. Filming your own behind-the-scenes.

Yeon: Drive with nowhere to go turns into bossiness. We've all seen it. In you. Last Tuesday.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Spend the extra on {helper_el}: make something. Bossiness is wasted fuel.

wealth.title: What keeps you balanced on a comeback: {helper_el}
wealth.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. Yours is strong and already expressive, so what balances you is {helper_el}, the element you shape.

Bom: In group life that means concrete goals. A target for this comeback. A skill to finish. A stage you want to own.

Yeon: Aim it. Talent without a target is just very loud wandering.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balance is {helper_el}: one clear goal per comeback. Written down.

wood.text: Wood, practice-room version: long stretches, morning walks, a plant in the dorm, learning a new style from zero. Growth you can feel week to week.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood for you: a plant on the windowsill and one new skill.

fire.text: Fire, practice-room version: sunlight, warm-ups with the music way too loud, and the member who makes you laugh until you can't breathe.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fire for you: loud warm-ups and the funniest person in the building.

earth.text: Earth, practice-room version: routine, home cooking, the same café every week, a manager you trust, sleeping in your own bed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth for you: routine, real meals, your own pillow.

metal.text: Metal, practice-room version: clean lines, a tidy bag, one-take vocal goals, and cancelling the extra schedule you said yes to out of guilt.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal for you: cancel one thing you agreed to out of guilt.

water.text: Water, practice-room version: quiet, night walks, long showers, journaling after a show, a playlist nobody else knows exists.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water for you: a night walk and a playlist that's only yours.

rat.text:
There's a box under your bed. Every handwritten letter you've ever got is in it. You've never mentioned it.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Rat, 子, midnight Water: quick, private, secretly sentimental.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat underneath: you keep every letter. Don't even try to deny it.

ox.text:
Same snack, same bedtime, same argument about whose turn it is to take the bins out.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold winter Earth: steady, routine-loving, stubborn about fairness.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox underneath: you'd win the bins argument with a dated spreadsheet.

tiger.text:
It's midnight and you're trying to talk three members into a run to the river.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early spring Wood: restless, brave, bored by a quiet dorm in about nine minutes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger underneath: every quiet night is a dare you haven't taken yet.

rabbit.text:
Best skincare shelf in the dorm. Soft lighting. A mirror you've positioned on purpose.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, spring Wood, one of the peach-blossom branches saju links with charm. Soft, aesthetic, a tiny bit vain.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit underneath: soft, pretty, slightly vain. Correctly vain.

dragon.text:
Big personality, sweatpants, three stories at once, and somehow all of them are true.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp Earth that stores Water: full of plans, harder to read than you look.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon underneath: loud on the surface, a whole basement of feelings below.

snake.text:
You've watched the whole argument without a word. Then one sentence, and it's over.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Snake, 巳, early summer Fire: observant, a little mysterious, noticing everything.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake underneath: you saw it all. You said one thing. It was enough.

horse.text:
"Rest day" to you means a market, a café, a park and dinner somewhere new. Before 3pm.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire, another peach-blossom branch: warm, loud, impossible to keep indoors.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse underneath: you've never once rested on a rest day.

goat.text:
Blanket. Sketchbook. A drama you're rewatching for the fourth time. Do not disturb.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth: gentle, artistic, a professional homebody.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat underneath: fourth rewatch, still cried at episode nine.

monkey.text:
You invented a dorm game. Everyone says they hate it. Everyone plays it every night.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Monkey, 申, early autumn Metal: clever, fidgety, fixing gadgets nobody asked you to fix.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey underneath: you took the TV remote apart "to improve it".

rooster.text:
3am, fire alarm drill. You walk out with perfect hair. Nobody understands how.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Rooster, 酉, autumn Metal, the last peach-blossom branch: neat, precise, quietly proud of the details.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster underneath: camera-ready at 3am. Suspicious, honestly.

dog.text:
You know every member's birthday, their mum's birthday and the dog's birthday.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth that keeps Fire: fiercely loyal, the first to defend the group in the comments.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog underneath: you've argued with strangers online for the group. Twice this week.

pig.text:
Asleep on the couch, the van, a bean bag, once standing up. Sharing snacks the whole time.

Your day branch shows the you only close people see. Yours is the Pig, 亥, early winter Water: easygoing, generous, comfortable anywhere.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig underneath: generous, sleepy, everyone's favourite pillow.

day_branch_heading: After lights out: the {day_animal} ({day_branch}) under your chart

plan.text:
You said you're the one with the plan. Of course you did. The spreadsheet has tabs.

{pos} with a planner brain means a clipboard lives in your head: the schedule, the formation, the backup plan if the backup fails.

Bom: Groups trust people like you with the hard stuff.

Yeon: Make sure you also get the fun stuff. You're not the group's admin assistant.

Bom: Share the plan early. Planners keep the whole picture in their heads and members end up feeling managed instead of included.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They'd hand you the schedule by week two. You'd colour-code it by week three.

mood.text:
You said you keep it fun. In K-pop terms that's the mood maker: every group needs one, few give them enough credit.

{pos} plus mood maker means you're why a fourteen-hour shoot doesn't feel like fourteen hours.

Yeon: Notice when you're joking so you don't have to say something real.

Bom: Mood makers burn out quietly, behind the jokes.

Yeon: Book one day where nobody needs you to be funny. Not one bit.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mood maker. Just don't joke your way past your own feelings.

quiet.text:
You said you quietly do the hard part. The load-bearing wall of the group, basically.

{pos} plus quiet worker means your work holds the whole thing up and asks for zero applause.

Bom: Ask for a little anyway. Credit isn't greed.

Yeon: "I fixed the harmony in the bridge" is information. It isn't bragging. Say it at the meeting.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fans find the quiet workers late. Then they never shut up about them.

shine.text:
You said you present it and shine. Center behaviour, whatever the official chart says.

{pos} plus spotlight means you're the face people remember from the group photo.

Bom: Enjoy it. And thank the member who made the slides. Out loud. By name.

Yeon: Then practise the boring parts with the same sparkle. Shine lasts longer on solid basics.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Shine away. Then credit whoever built the slides.

unsaid.text:
You skipped the group project question. Which is its own answer.

Some people hate being sorted. Fair. Your chart put your soul at {pos}, so read this as a guess at how you'd play it, and argue with it in the group chat.

Yeon: Here's a test. Next group chat argument, notice what role you slip into without trying.

Bom: That's your real position. You don't need to tell us. We'll know.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Skipped it. Mysterious. We respect it. We're also suspicious.

voice.text:
You'd want to be famous for your voice. Heard more than watched.

Saju ties the voice to Metal, the element of resonance, and to how freely your expression flows.

Bom: Sing in the shower louder this week. Seriously.

Yeon: Record yourself once a week. Not to judge. Just to hear how your voice shifts with your mood. It's a weirdly honest diary.

Bom: Next page: the fans. And what they'd quietly worry about.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Heard more than watched. That says a lot about you.

moves.text:
You'd want to be famous for your moves. Wood and Fire territory: growth, rhythm, getting the feeling out through the body.

{pos} plus mover means you think best while moving.

Yeon: Take your next hard decision on a walk. Not on your bed, scrolling.

Bom: Learn one short dance this month just for joy. Movement is how you process things. Give it a regular slot.

Yeon: Next page: your fans. They've already clipped your best eight counts.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You think with your body. Walk out your next big decision.

look.text:
You'd want to be famous for your look. No shame. Visual is a real position and it's harder than it looks.

It says you care how things land at first sight.

Bom: Make sure the look has your personality in it, not just this month's trend.

Yeon: Pick one signature detail. A ring, a hair clip, the way you roll your sleeves. Wear it everywhere. Signatures beat trends.

Bom: Turn the page. Your fans have opinions about that ring.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Visual is real work. Make the look yours, not the algorithm's.

words.text:
You'd want to be famous for your words. The writer member. The lyrics, the captions, the line that ends up on fan banners.

{pos} plus writer means your real superpower might be explaining people to themselves.

Yeon: Keep a notes file of lines you love, yours and other people's.

Bom: Writers get famous for the file, not for the lightning bolt.

Yeon: Next page: your fans, holding banners with your words on them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your line would end up on a banner in row three. Write more.

unsaid.text:
You didn't pick what you'd be famous for. Maybe you'd rather not be famous at all.

Bom: Honestly the healthiest answer in this whole reading.

Your chart still gave your soul a position. You can play it in a friend group instead of a stadium.

Yeon: Fame is optional. Knowing your position is the fun part. Next page: the fans you'd have anyway.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No interest in fame? Possibly the wisest answer in the whole quiz.

wood.heading: Your stage energy: growth
wood.text:
Bom: Wood members get better in public. Fans can see the whole curve: the shaky debut, the confident third comeback.

Yeon: The "then vs now" compilation of you is a genre.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You grow in public. Fans love watching the curve.

fire.heading: Your stage energy: heat
fire.text:
Yeon: Fire members don't perform. They ignite. The ending fairy alone needs a content warning.

Bom: You give everything on stage. Save a little for after.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your ending fairy broke the internet. Twice.

earth.heading: Your stage energy: anchor
earth.text:
Bom: Earth members hold the formation together. When someone slips, you cover it before anyone notices.

Yeon: Fans call you "the stable one". In fancams, you're the one never off-beat.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're the reason the formation never falls apart.

metal.heading: Your stage energy: precision
metal.text:
Yeon: Metal members hit every mark. Sharp angles, clean lines, zero wasted movement.

Bom: Dance teachers use your practice videos as the example. That's respect.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your choreo is so clean it should be illegal.

water.heading: Your stage energy: flow
water.text:
Bom: Water members move like the music is coming from inside them. Fluid, unpredictable, hypnotic.

Yeon: You also forget the choreo and freestyle. Fans call it "artistry". The choreographer calls it something else.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't dance the song. You become it.

peer.heading: Your signature move (fans have a name for it)
peer.text:
Your signature move is the huddle. You start it before every stage. Nobody remembers voting for that.

Yeon: Shoulder bump after a hard part. The hand you grab for the final bow.

Bom: Your chart's loudest element is your own, so you perform best as part of a unit. Fans would call it your members-first thing.

On a solo stage, talk to the band and the dancers like they're members too. You'll feel it click.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You start the huddle. Every time. Nobody even questions it anymore.

output.heading: Your signature move (fans have a name for it)
output.text:
Your signature move is the ad-lib. A run nobody rehearsed. A face that becomes a meme by Thursday.

Bom: Your chart's loudest element is the one you produce, so things spill out of you. Directors learn to leave you room.

Yeon: Your best stages are slightly off script. Your worst are very off script.

Keep a few go-to ad-libs ready so the freedom always has somewhere to land.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The ad-lib nobody rehearsed. Directors learned to leave you a gap.

wealth.heading: Your signature move (fans have a name for it)
wealth.text:
Your signature move is the clean finish. Final pose, a beat early, held like you own the building.

Bom: Your chart's loudest element is the one you control, so you care about results people can see. And the ending is where a stage gets judged.

Yeon: Fans screenshot your last frame. Every comeback.

Finish every rehearsal run fully, even the tired ones. Same instinct, more reps.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Last pose, first to land, longest held. Screenshot material.

power.heading: Your signature move (fans have a name for it)
power.text:
Your signature move is control. A stop timed to the millisecond. A live vocal that doesn't shake in the hardest choreo.

Bom: Your chart's loudest element is the one that presses on you, so this comes from discipline. Fans can feel the hours.

Yeon: Let them see the hours, too. A sweaty, grinning bow after a brutal stage is half the appeal.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Control is your move. Let them see the sweat sometimes.

resource.heading: Your signature move (fans have a name for it)
resource.text:
Your signature move is the quiet glance. Two seconds into the lens, like you know something the audience doesn't.

Bom: Your chart's loudest element is the one that feeds you, so you perform from the inside out. Stillness reads as depth.

Yeon: Fans would write essays about a two-second close-up. Footnotes included.

Throw in one big moment now and then, so the quiet ones keep their power.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Two seconds of eye contact and the essays begin.

spring.heading: What your fandom would be like
spring.text:
Spring-born, so your fandom feels like spring. Young, hopeful, growing fast.

Bom: They find you early and recruit everyone they know. Colourful fan art, chants a little out of sync and loud anyway.

Yeon: Keep handing them firsts. First live. First cover. First time you tell a real story.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring fandom: found you first, recruited their whole school.

summer.heading: What your fandom would be like
summer.text:
Summer-born, so your fandom is loud. One colour filling a stadium, singing the chorus louder than you.

Bom: They love spectacle and big feelings. Every comeback, every festival, there.

Yeon: Return the heat. A shouted thank-you mid-song goes further than a polished speech.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer fandom: louder than the speakers. Yell thanks back.

autumn.heading: What your fandom would be like
autumn.text:
Autumn-born, so your fandom is thoughtful and loyal. They stay through the quiet years.

Bom: They notice everything. A change in your handwriting. A new ring. A lyric that sounds too personal.

Yeon: Respect that attention by being real with them. They'll outlast any trend.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn fandom: noticed the new ring before your manager did.

winter.heading: What your fandom would be like
winter.text:
Winter-born, so your fandom starts small and fiercely protective. A secret club with good snacks.

Bom: Warm letters, careful birthday projects, quiet but firm defence online.

Yeon: Slow to warm up. Then they never leave. Give them late-night lives and a song written for them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter fandom: small, loyal, permanent. They'd want a song.

earth.heading: What your fandom would be like
earth.text:
Born in the Earth days between seasons, so your fandom is the steady kind. Every age, every background, held together by trust more than hype.

Bom: Charity projects in your name. Just as happy at a tiny event as a stadium.

Yeon: Keep even the tiny promises. The cover you mentioned once in 2024? They remember.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Earth-days fandom: steady, loyal, and they remember every promise.

output.heading: The thing you dodge in every fight
output.text:
With the output element missing from your visible chart, the thing you dodge is the feeling itself.

Yeon: You'll explain the facts. The schedule. The reasons. And skip the part where you were hurt.

Bom: Members end up arguing with your logic while the real thing sits there untouched.

Open with one feeling word. Annoyed. Embarrassed. Left out. It changes the whole conversation.

Yeon: Next page: your blind spot. The one you'd argue about.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with the feeling word. The facts can wait their turn.

wealth.heading: The thing you dodge in every fight
wealth.text:
With the wealth element missing from your visible chart, the thing you dodge is asking for the outcome you want.

Bom: You'll describe what went wrong in detail and stop right before what should happen next.

Yeon: So they can't fix it. They don't know what fixed looks like.

End every complaint with a request: "Next time, can we...".

Bom: And next page, your blind spot. Yeon has been waiting all reading for this one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Describe what fixed looks like. Nobody can hit a target they can't see.

power.heading: The thing you dodge in every fight
power.text:
With the power element missing from your visible chart, the thing you dodge is the rule underneath.

Yeon: You fight about the incident and never agree on the principle. So the same fight comes back next month in a new outfit.

Bom: After you make up, agree on one small house rule together.

Boring. It works.

Yeon: Next page: your blind spot. Bring a snack. It's a long one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same fight, new outfit? Agree one small rule afterwards.

resource.heading: The thing you dodge in every fight
resource.text:
With the resource element missing from your visible chart, the thing you dodge is being comforted.

Bom: You'd rather sort it out alone than let a member see you upset.

Yeon: They feel shut out and try harder, which feels like pressure, so you hide harder. Lovely loop.

Let one person sit with you while you're upset. No fixing. That's the whole assignment.

Bom: Next page, your blind spot. We'll be gentle. Yeon won't.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Let someone sit with you. No fixing allowed.

none.heading: The thing you dodge in every fight
none.text:
All five elements show up in your chart, so there's no single obvious hole in how you fight.

Bom: You can argue, listen, compromise, make up. Rare.

Yeon: What you dodge is choosing. You see every side so clearly you never land on your own.

Say which side you're on, even if it's only sixty percent.

Yeon: Next page: the blind spot. Yes, even you have one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Every side makes sense to you. Choose one anyway. Sixty percent is enough.

wood.heading: Your solo era wardrobe
wood.text:
Your balancing element is Wood, so the solo wants Wood styling. Sage to forest green, linen, soft tailoring, long lines, plants and morning light on set.

Bom: Wood tells fans you're growing. That's exactly the story a solo debut should tell.

Yeon: One more song after this. The encore. Don't leave yet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Sage, linen, morning light. A growing-up story.

fire.heading: Your solo era wardrobe
fire.text:
Your balancing element is Fire, so the solo wants Fire styling. Reds and warm coral, satin that catches the lights, bold shoulders, candles or neon or a sunset on set.

Yeon: Fire worn shyly looks wrong. Wear it like you mean it.

Bom: And stay for the encore. One more song, the most honest one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Satin, coral, bold shoulders. No shy Fire allowed.

earth.heading: Your solo era wardrobe
earth.text:
Your balancing element is Earth, so the solo wants Earth styling. Camel, sand, terracotta, cream. Knitwear, soft leather, a warm wooden room.

Bom: You look approachable. The solo artist people want to have dinner with.

Yeon: Encore next. One more song. Bom has been saving something.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Camel and terracotta. Dinner-invitation aesthetic.

metal.heading: Your solo era wardrobe
metal.text:
Your balancing element is Metal, so the solo wants Metal styling. White, silver, grey, crisp black, sharp tailoring, one statement piece of jewellery, a clean almost futuristic set.

Yeon: Edit the outfit until removing anything would break it.

Bom: Then the encore. Last song. Stay.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Crisp, minimal, one statement piece. Edit hard.

water.heading: Your solo era wardrobe
water.text:
Your balancing element is Water, so the solo wants Water styling. Navy, black, deep blue, fabric that moves, wet-look hair, sea or rain or city lights at night.

Bom: Let the visuals be a little hard to read. Mystery suits you.

Yeon: Don't close the tab. The encore's next, and it's about you, not the idol.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Navy, flowing fabric, rain on the lens.

yang.heading: The last word: you're yang
yang.text:
Your Day Master is yang, the outward half of saju's pair. You fill space. You go first. You're easy to spot from the back of an arena.

Bom: That's a gift, as long as you remember the quieter members are working just as hard in a lower register.

Yeon: Some of the best moments on any stage happen when a yang member steps back and lets someone else glow.

Bom: That's the reading. You were never just a position. You're the reason the group works. Curtain.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You go first. Step back once and watch someone else light up.

yin.heading: The last word: you're yin
yin.text:
Your Day Master is yin, the inward half of saju's pair. You don't reach out. You draw people in. Fans lean closer to hear you.

Bom: That's a gift, as long as you never mistake quiet for less important.

Yeon: Some of the strongest moments on stage are a yin member taking the center unexpectedly and owning every second.

Bom: That's the reading. Whatever spot they'd give you, the group would feel the gap if you left. Curtain.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: People lean in for you. Take the center once and keep it.

rat.heading: The clip that converts people
rat.text: With the Rat under your chart: one clever line in an interview, and the host laughs so hard the camera shakes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One line. Crying host. Shaky camera. Career-defining.

ox.heading: The clip that converts people
ox.text: With the Ox under your chart: quietly carrying the heaviest equipment box at a fan event while everyone else poses for photos.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Carrying the heavy boxes while others pose. Fans saw.

tiger.heading: The clip that converts people
tiger.text: With the Tiger under your chart: jumping into a dance challenge you've never practised and nailing it on the first try.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Never practised it, nailed it anyway. Annoying. Iconic.

rabbit.heading: The clip that converts people
rabbit.text: With the Rabbit under your chart: a sleepy airport outfit photo that gets more likes than the music video.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: An airport photo beating the music video. Classic Rabbit.

dragon.heading: The clip that converts people
dragon.text: With the Dragon under your chart: telling a wild story on a variety show that turns out to be one hundred percent true.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The wild story was true. Every single word. Fans checked.

snake.heading: The clip that converts people
snake.text: With the Snake under your chart: one slow, knowing look into a fancam lens, replayed until the video glitches.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One slow look into the lens. Replayed until it glitched.

horse.heading: The clip that converts people
horse.text: With the Horse under your chart: sprinting the whole length of the stage in the encore to high-five the far seats.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Full sprint to the cheap seats. Security did not sign off on that.

goat.heading: The clip that converts people
goat.text: With the Goat under your chart: a hand-drawn gift for a member, shown by accident on a live.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The drawing was supposed to be a secret. Now it's merch.

monkey.heading: The clip that converts people
monkey.text: With the Monkey under your chart: a prank on the leader so elaborate the leader stops and applauds.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A prank so good the victim clapped. That's talent.

rooster.heading: The clip that converts people
rooster.text: With the Rooster under your chart: fixing a member's collar mid-song with a perfectly straight face.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Collar fixed mid-chorus. Not even a smile. Fans screamed.

dog.heading: The clip that converts people
dog.text: With the Dog under your chart: stepping in when a member gets an awkward question and answering it for them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Took the awkward question for a member. Loyal to the bone.

pig.heading: The clip that converts people
pig.text: With the Pig under your chart: asleep on a member's shoulder at a long award show, live on the big screen.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Napping on the big screen at an award show. Peak Pig.

peer.heading: You as a roommate, honestly reviewed
peer.text:
Yeon: You'd split the room fifty-fifty. Down to the centimetre. With tape.

Bom: Fair, generous with shared snacks, slightly territorial about your side.

Best with a roommate who has their own strong routine, so neither of you feels managed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tape line down the middle of the room. Fair, though.

output.heading: You as a roommate, honestly reviewed
output.text:
Bom: The fun roommate. Music on, half-finished craft projects on the desk, friends dropping by at strange hours.

Yeon: Everyone loves living with you. Until they need to sleep.

Agree on quiet hours in week one and you stay the favourite.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fun roommate. Set quiet hours early and keep the crown.

wealth.heading: You as a roommate, honestly reviewed
wealth.text:
Yeon: Labelled containers. A shared calendar. A plan for the electricity bill with a colour key.

Bom: Life runs smoother for everyone near you.

It can also feel like living with a manager. Leave one corner deliberately messy, as a peace offering.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One messy corner. On purpose. Diplomacy.

power.heading: You as a roommate, honestly reviewed
power.text:
Bom: The responsible roommate. Up on time, bed made, nothing borrowed without asking.

Yeon: Roommates feel safe with you. And very slightly judged.

Laugh at your own rules sometimes. It tells everyone they're allowed to be human around you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Reliable roommate. Let them catch you being silly too.

resource.heading: You as a roommate, honestly reviewed
resource.text:
Bom: The cosy roommate. Blankets, books, tea at midnight, and a real talent for listening.

Yeon: People bring you their problems. You've become an unlicensed therapist with good tea.

Keep the room a place where you recharge too, not only a free counselling service.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Free tea, free therapy. Start charging in naps.

spring.heading: Your comeback week
spring.text:
Spring-born members hit comeback week like a sprint start. Fast out of the blocks, buzzing with stage ideas.

Yeon: By the fourth music show, you're running on fumes and fan chants.

Bom: Save one new detail, a different ad-lib, a new expression, for week two. Keeps it fresh for you.

Yeon: Next page: your solo era. I planned it. You're welcome.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Spring start: save one surprise for week two.

summer.heading: Your comeback week
summer.text:
Summer-born members thrive in comeback chaos. Early calls, back-to-back stages, fans everywhere. You run hot and happy.

Yeon: The crash comes after. It always comes after.

Bom: Block the day after the last music show for nothing at all. Defend it like a contract clause.

Yeon: Then turn the page. Your solo era is waiting, and it's loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You run hot. Book the crash day before the crash books you.

autumn.heading: Your comeback week
autumn.text:
Autumn-born members treat comeback week like harvest. Everything you practised finally pays off and you want every stage clean.

Yeon: Which means one tiny mistake and you're replaying it in the van.

Bom: Watch one stage back purely for joy. No notes allowed.

Yeon: Next page: the solo era. I made a moodboard.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Harvest week: rewatch one stage for joy only.

winter.heading: Your comeback week
winter.text:
Winter-born members start slow and finish strong. Stage one feels stiff. The last one feels like flying.

Bom: Don't judge the whole comeback on day one.

Yeon: Your best performance usually lands when everyone else is already wrecked. Smug, but earned.

Bom: Next page: your solo era. It starts quiet, too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Slow warm-up, best stage last. Day one is not the verdict.

earth.heading: Your comeback week
earth.text:
Born in the Earth days, you pace comeback week perfectly. Same warm-up, same meal, same bedtime. Every day.

Bom: Members borrow your calm without asking.

Yeon: Share the routine with whoever's spiralling. More useful than any pep talk.

Bom: Then turn the page. Your solo era, planned by Yeon, who refused to let me pick the colours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your boring routine is the group's emergency kit.

output.heading: The member you need next to you
output.text:
Your chart is short on its output element, so the member you need beside you is the expressive one. The person who says what they feel without editing.

Bom: Standing next to them gives you permission to do the same.

Yeon: Every group has one. Sit next to them at dinner. Steal their honesty.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sit next to the most expressive member. Honesty is contagious.

wealth.heading: The member you need next to you
wealth.text:
Your chart is short on its wealth element, so the member you need beside you is the ambitious one. The person who says "let's ask for that part" and means it.

Bom: They'll pull you toward chances you'd let drift past.

Yeon: Let them be a bit pushy with you. You need it. You know you need it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Keep the ambitious one close. Let them shove a little.

power.heading: The member you need next to you
power.text:
Your chart is short on its power element, so the member you need beside you is the disciplined one. Knows the call time, knows the formation, reminds you of both.

Yeon: That isn't nagging. It's structure, borrowed from a friend.

Bom: Say thank you once. They hear a lot of sighing.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The strict member isn't nagging. That's borrowed structure, free of charge.

resource.heading: The member you need next to you
resource.text:
Your chart is short on its resource element, so the member you need beside you is the gentle one. Notices you're tired. Puts a snack in your bag.

Bom: Let them. Being looked after is the support your chart doesn't bring on its own.

Yeon: Stop saying "you didn't have to". They know. They wanted to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A snack appears in your bag. Say thanks, not "you didn't have to".

none.heading: The member you need next to you
none.text:
With all five elements in your chart, you get along with nearly anyone. So the member you need is simply the one who tells you the truth.

Yeon: Range makes people agreeable. Agreeable people collect yes-men.

Bom: Keep one person who'll say "that wasn't your best stage" and still sit with you after.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Easy with everyone? Keep one brutally honest friend.

wood.heading: You in the practice room
wood.text:
Wood in the practice room: you stretch longer than anyone and set a tiny goal every session. One count to clean, one note to hit. Written down.

Yeon: Now, about the answers you gave us at the start. They said more than you meant them to. Next page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One small goal per session, written down. Progress you can see.

fire.heading: You in the practice room
fire.text:
Fire in the practice room: music loud, everyone dripping, and you're the one shouting "one more run!" when the others are done. Great for the group. Terrible for your knees. Cool down properly.

Yeon: Also, your answers at the start gave you away. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "One more run." Then an actual cool-down. Both.

earth.heading: You in the practice room
earth.text:
Earth in the practice room: same spot on the floor, same water bottle, same warm-up order every day. Members set their timing by you.

Bom: And the two answers you gave us at the start? We read them very closely. Next page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same spot, same order. Members time themselves by you.

metal.heading: You in the practice room
metal.text:
Metal in the practice room: you film every run and study it like evidence, counting the frames where an arm came in late. The group is cleaner because of you.

Yeon: I studied your answers the same way. Findings on the next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You film everything and count late frames. The forensics department.

water.heading: You in the practice room
water.text:
Water in the practice room: late at night, building empty, lights low, improvising until something new shows up. Leave yourself a note before bed or the idea floats off.

Bom: Speaking of things you let slip: your answers. Next page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Late night, lights low. Write the idea down before it drifts.

gap-wood.text:
People watch your fancam for the formations. You dance and quietly steer a member half a step left for the whole song.

Yeon: Top comment: "how are they dancing AND supervising".

Bom: Then the bridge drops and you stand completely still for two counts. A tree doesn't have to move to be noticed.

Yeon: Those two counts of nothing are the screenshot.

Bom: Homework: once per stage, stop checking on everyone and look straight down the lens.

Yeon: Next page, your elements as a setlist. One track is way too loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're always the frame. Be the photo for once.

gap-wood.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

eul-wood.text:
Your best fancam isn't from the big title track stage. It's a small festival, wet floor, rain.

Bom: You couldn't do the slide, so you improvised. And invented a better version.

Yeon: Fans would timestamp everything. The finger flick at 1:42. The hair you "accidentally" let fall.

Bom: Vines adapt to whatever wall they're given. Bad conditions turn into new moves.

Yeon: So stop apologising for the improvised bits. They're the only clips anyone keeps.

Bom: Turn the page. Your elements, played as a setlist.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The slippery stage made your best clip. Remember that next time something goes wrong.

eul-wood.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

byeong-fire.text:
Your fancam barely needs a camera operator. The frame just drifts toward you like a plant to a window.

Yeon: You smile at the lens in the hardest dance break and people forget the dance break exists.

Bom: But watch the half second before your center line. One sharp breath. Your face goes completely serious.

Yeon: That flicker is the real clip. Most people scroll past it.

Bom: Let the serious second stay a little longer. Brightness gets views. Brightness with focus in it gets loyalty.

Yeon: Next: your elements as a setlist. Spoiler, one of them is on repeat.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The breath before the smile. That's the part they fall for.

byeong-fire.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

jeong-fire.text:
Your fancam is a vocal fancam, which is a rare genre. People turn the volume up instead of watching the feet.

Yeon: The comments are all timestamps. "2:58 the ad-lib." "3:10 the breath." "not even nervous??"

Bom: You'd watch it once, wince at something only you can hear, and close the app.

Yeon: New rule. Watch it twice. Once as the critic. Once as the fan who rode a bus four hours to hear you.

Bom: The candle can't see its own glow. It needs the view from the seats.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, played as a setlist. Bring tea.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Second viewing: from seat 34F. Try it.

jeong-fire.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

mu-earth.text:
Your fancam is the one other singers share. Quietly. In group chats.

Bom: You rarely get the flashy line. You get the low harmony that makes the flashy line possible.

Yeon: Fans find your cam years late, then lose an entire weekend in the archive.

Bom: "How did I not notice the mountain" is a whole genre of comment.

Yeon: The fix isn't louder. Pick one moment per song that's only yours. A held note. A step forward on the last chorus.

Bom: Mountains get photographed when they catch the light. Next page, your elements as a setlist.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pick your sunrise. One moment per song.

mu-earth.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

gi-earth.text:
Trainees learn the choreography from your fancam. You do every move fully, even the boring transitions others mark.

Yeon: Then the encore cam. Formation gone, song looping, and you're picking up a fan letter, fixing a mic and still singing verse two.

Bom: Comment section calls it "the all-rounder cam". Six jobs in four minutes.

Yeon: Lovely. Also a warning.

Bom: Try one encore where you have exactly one job: enjoying it. The garden won't collapse while you dance in it.

Yeon: Next page: your elements as a setlist. Yours has a track you keep skipping.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One encore, zero jobs. Just you, dancing badly on purpose.

gi-earth.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

gyeong-metal.text:
Your fancam starts when your verse does. Until then you're half in shadow, marking, saving it.

Yeon: Then the beat switches and you step out like a blade leaving the sheath. Chin down, eyes up, every syllable on the grid.

Bom: Caption: "zero to dangerous in one bar".

Yeon: The part that actually goes viral is after. You step back into formation and grin at the member beside you.

Bom: Don't hide the grin to protect the cool image. Sharp plus warm is rarer than sharp alone.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, as a setlist. Some of it I'd cut.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keep the grin. The scary face is common. The grin isn't.

gyeong-metal.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

sin-metal.text:
Your fancam has the highest view count and the most argued-over thumbnail.

Bom: You read the camera like a jeweller reads light. You find the angle without looking.

Yeon: And you feel every flaw in that clip. The rushed step. The hair. The expression you held a beat too long.

Bom: Pressure is what cuts a jewel. Your inner editor supplies plenty.

Yeon: Keep the standard. Drop the punishment. Write down one thing to polish, then close the app.

Bom: You're polishing, not repairing. Next page: your elements, as a setlist.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One note to self. Then close the app. That's the whole rule.

sin-metal.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

im-water.text:
Your fancam is a strange one. Fans love it for exactly that.

Bom: You sing everyone else's parts under your breath, because you wrote half of them.

Yeon: In the instrumental bridge you nod slightly off-beat. Turns out it's the beat of a counter-melody only you can hear.

Bom: Fans figure it out years later from a studio vlog. The fancam goes viral twice.

Yeon: On stage you're mixing the track in your head. Stop. Perform one song a night as a listener.

Bom: Let the crowd hear what you built. Next page: your elements, played as a setlist.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Stop adjusting the levels mid-stage. Nobody can hear the hi-hat but you.

im-water.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

gye-water.text:
Your fancam is the chaos cam. Waving at a fan sign during the serious bridge. Swapping a move with a member mid-song.

Yeon: Blowing a kiss at a camera operator who was not ready. The comments are just keyboard smashes.

Bom: And yet. You never miss your actual part. The mischief happens around the edges, and the line lands right on time.

Yeon: Lightness with discipline underneath. That's rarer than they think.

Bom: When the company says "be more mature on stage", smile and keep half the mischief.

Yeon: Next page: your elements as a setlist. Even your chart is a bit chaotic.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mischief on the edges, line dead on time. That's the formula.

gye-water.heading: Your fancam (the clip that goes viral)

gap-wood.text:
Cooking segment. You assign everyone a job in four seconds flat.

Bom: Then you burn the rice.

Yeon: In HD. You'll be explaining that rice for five years.

Bom: You answer every silly question for real. "If you were a vegetable" gets two thoughtful minutes on broccoli and teamwork.

Yeon: The straight face is the joke. You still haven't figured that out.

Bom: A leader who laughs at the burnt rice is one people relax around.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lean into the rice. It's your most relatable content.

gap-wood.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

eul-wood.text:
You don't fight for airtime on variety. You sit slightly to the side and react.

Yeon: One raised eyebrow at a member's terrible joke. The editors make it the thumbnail.

Bom: Then random play dance. A girl group song from 2009.

Yeon: You stand up, do the entire routine perfectly with zero expression, and sit back down. Studio destroyed.

Bom: Your reactions are funny. Your participation is legendary. Say yes to the silly games.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The eyebrow got its own subtitle font.

eul-wood.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

byeong-fire.text:
You're the main character of the episode before the opening credits finish.

Yeon: You laugh at your own story before the punchline. The host laughs anyway. Unfair.

Bom: Producers love you at hour nine of filming, when everyone else is a zombie.

Yeon: The risk: you carry the whole episode and the other members turn into background.

Bom: The episode where you grow up is the one where you hand the mic to the quietest member. "Tell them about Osaka."

Yeon: Then you shut up and let them get the laugh. Revolutionary.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Setting up someone else's punchline: still counts as your win.

byeong-fire.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

jeong-fire.text:
On variety you start shy and end dangerous.

Bom: Twenty minutes of polite smiling and "yes, I like that too".

Yeon: Then someone teases you once too often and a deadpan line comes out so sharp the host has to stop filming.

Bom: Then the letter-to-your-parents segment. You try very hard not to cry. You fail beautifully.

Yeon: Five minutes later, another deadpan line. The whiplash is the brand.

Bom: Don't fight either one. Range is the most charming thing a candle can show.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The candle has a hot tip. Hosts keep forgetting.

jeong-fire.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

mu-earth.text:
Variety shows give you every physical challenge. Heavy box, plank, tug of war.

Yeon: You do it with a calm face while everyone else screams. That's the joke.

Bom: Then the quiz. Obscure history question. Silence. You answer it.

Yeon: Because you read constantly and have never once mentioned it.

Bom: Fans start calling you "the secret encyclopedia" by the next morning.

Yeon: People only see the side you show. Show the dry jokes and the weird hobbies. The cave is the interesting part of the mountain.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Strongest in the tug of war, smartest in the quiz. Let them see both.

mu-earth.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

gi-earth.text:
You quietly make the variety show work. The youngest is nervous, so you feed them an easy question.

Bom: The host's joke flops. You laugh anyway. Snacks between takes.

Yeon: Then the ranking game. Solo challenge. Nobody to help.

Bom: And you turn out to be ruthless. Cheerfully, kindly ruthless.

Yeon: Fans will never recover. The soil grows thorns when it wants to.

Bom: Win something on camera without apologising to the people you beat. Nice and competitive aren't opposites.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Smiling sweetly while eliminating three members. Best episode of the season.

gi-earth.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

gyeong-metal.text:
You on variety: the scary rapper who is catastrophically bad at anything cute.

Yeon: The aegyo segment. Stiff, focused, a face like you're defusing a bomb. That clip outlives every serious stage you've done.

Bom: Then the truth game. "Who's the messiest member?" Instant answer. With evidence.

Yeon: Hosts love you because you don't dodge.

Bom: Your bluntness is funnier with a smile. Same words, softer face.

Yeon: People take a lot of truth if it comes with a laugh. Swords look friendlier cutting cake.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Defusing a bomb, but it's a heart gesture. Iconic.

gyeong-metal.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

sin-metal.text:
The variety show expects you to sit there and look good. Then you open your mouth.

Yeon: "What's your charm point?" "My left elbow." No explanation. Ever.

Bom: Then a game you lose badly. Flour penalty. Face covered.

Yeon: The jewel, coated in flour, still posing. Fans adopt that clip as a national treasure.

Bom: It shows you can be imperfect and completely fine.

Yeon: Say yes to the messy games. The polished image gets admired. The flour face gets loved.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Flour face, perfect pose. More loved than any photo shoot.

sin-metal.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

im-water.text:
The host asks your favourite food. Twelve minutes later you're explaining why a chord progression tastes like ramen at 2am.

Yeon: Somehow it makes sense. The editors use a tiny subtitle font just to keep up.

Bom: You shine in the music segments. Make a song in ten minutes? Done in seven.

Yeon: Outside those, you're staring at the lighting rig thinking about reverb.

Bom: That's fine. The ocean doesn't perform on the surface all day.

Yeon: Just come up for the group photo at the end. You missed it last time.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Seven minutes, one song, everyone stunned. Then you wander off.

im-water.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

gye-water.text:
You're why the episode trends. You prank the host and steal the leader's snack mid-sentence.

Yeon: You lose games on purpose so you can do the penalty dance.

Bom: The older members pretend to be exhausted by you. They laugh hardest.

Yeon: Then the camping episode. Late-night fire. You say something so thoughtful about the group that everyone goes silent.

Bom: Rain looks playful. It's also what keeps the forest alive.

Yeon: Let the deep one show up more than once a year. We liked them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Prankster at noon, philosopher by the campfire. Both are you.

gye-water.heading: You on a variety show (Yeon produces)

strong.heading: You versus the comment section
strong.text:
You read hate comments like a weather report. Notice, mutter, carry on.

Yeon: The danger isn't that they hurt. It's that you want to reply. A calm, devastating reply at 3am.

Bom: Don't. The company sighs, the fans fight for a week, and the commenter gets exactly the attention they wanted.

Use the backbone for the members who don't have one yet. When a quieter member gets hit by a rumour, you sit next to them in the van, take the phone away for the night and say "we know who you are". Your skin is thick. Lend it.

Yeon: And when the fight is inside the group, not in the comments? Next page. It's less flattering.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your thick skin is a loan service. Sit with whoever's hurting.

weak.heading: You versus the comment section
weak.text:
One nasty line about your face outweighs ten thousand kind ones. And you'll remember it word for word next year.

Bom: That isn't fragility. It's sensitivity, the same thing that makes you brilliant at reading a room.

Yeon: So build a filter. Walls are for people with worse taste.

Never read comments on the night of a stage, tired and wide open. Have one person you trust skim the reactions and send you only the good ones. Keep a folder of fan letters and actually open it on bad days. The person typing at 2am doesn't know you. The people in that folder do.

Bom: Now, the fights that happen inside the group. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Let someone you trust read the comments first. You read the letters.

plan.speaker: yeon
plan.text: "The one with the plan." So you made the group project spreadsheet. With colour codes. Nobody asked.

mood.speaker: bom
mood.text: "The one who keeps it fun." Every group needs a mood maker. Without you, it's just homework.

quiet.speaker: bom
quiet.text: "Quietly doing the hard part." The member fans discover in year three and never shut up about.

shine.speaker: yeon
shine.text: "The one who presents it and shines." You did 10 percent of the work and 100 percent of the applause. Iconic.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You skipped your group project role. Which means it's either "did everything" or "did nothing". We'll find out.

voice.speaker: bom
voice.text: Famous for your voice. The member whose live vocals make the comments section go "CD swallowed".

moves.speaker: yeon
moves.text: Famous for your moves. So the fancam with eleven million views is yours. Humble about it? No.

look.speaker: yeon
look.text: Famous for your look. The airport photos alone have their own fan account.

words.speaker: bom
words.text: Famous for your words. The member who writes the lyrics, the captions, and the 2am fan letters back.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: No pick for the fame question. Fine. Fans will decide. They always do.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

gap-wood.your-position:
You're the {pos_lower}. Not because you asked. Because when it all went wrong, everybody looked at you.

Bom: You speak for the group. You protect the younger ones.

Yeon: You also give the speech at every award show. Same speech. Fans can recite it.

Bom: Your real talent is making people feel safe enough to shine.
gap-wood.on-stage:
Bom: Because you're not performing at the crowd. You're checking on the youngest during the hard formation, and the camera catches the glance.

Yeon: One glance. Four million views. You were counting the line, not flirting with the lens.

Your in-ear dies mid-song. You cover the missing harmony so smoothly the audience never finds out.

Bom: You hold the shape so everyone else can sparkle inside it.

Yeon: Number of moments per song that are just yours: zero. We counted.
gap-wood.in-the-dorm:
1am. Everyone's asleep except you, rewriting the shower rota on the fridge whiteboard.

Bom: You make breakfast for whoever stumbles out first. Every single morning.

Yeon: You also do push-ups at 6am loud enough to count as an alarm.

Bom: And you cried at the dog movie last night.

Yeon: "Allergies." Sure. The members let you have that one.

Bom: They let you pretend because they know the soft part is the real part.
gap-wood.group-drama:
Someone was careless, and you took it personally on behalf of the entire group.

Yeon: Arms crossed, full meeting, "I just think it's unfair." Everyone saw it coming from the hallway.

Bom: Nobody ever has to wonder where they stand with you. That's rare.

Yeon: The catch: one late arrival becomes a Principle. And you do not bend on Principles.

Bom: Then you knock on their door first, with convenience store ramen and the most awkward speech ever written.

Yeon: Works every time. Mostly because the speech is so bad.
gap-wood.solo-era:
You go solo last. After you've checked the group can survive three months without you.

Bom: And when you do, it's a statement. A rooftop at dawn, you finally in the middle of the frame.

Yeon: Fans who filed you under "the reliable one" find out you had a whole personality on mute.

Bom: Your solo era is the version of you that was waiting for permission. Give it some.

gap-wood.speaker: bom
gap-wood.text: The tall pine. Obviously they made you leader.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: Leader energy. Also, unsolicited schedule-maker energy.

gap-wood.speaker: bom
gap-wood.text: You stand up straight, you speak first, you take the blame when it goes wrong.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: You watch the stage back and only see who was off-beat. Never yourself.

gap-wood.speaker: bom
gap-wood.text: Spare phone charger for every member. Labeled. Of course.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: You apologise first, bring snacks, and somehow still win the argument.

spring.intro: Spring birthday. That's tree season, so you got a double shot of yourself: taller, louder, surer. In saju terms, Wood ran the month you were born in. In real life, you've never once waited to be picked.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Double Wood. So the stubbornness is seasonal AND personal. Great.

summer.intro: You're a tree born in the heat. All that growing goes straight into showing: big plans, big talk, big gestures. Summer burns through a pine fast, so you look unstoppable right up until you suddenly need three days in bed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give off so much light. Just save a little for yourself.

earth.intro: Born in the between-season weeks, when soil runs the show. For a tree, that means work: you're always building, fixing, providing. Very useful. Very tired. Somebody should ask what you want for once.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rest is not a prize you win. It's allowed.

autumn.intro: Autumn is axe season, and you're the tree. Life started trimming you early: rules, pressure, people with opinions. It made you sharper and more disciplined than other pines. It also made you allergic to being told what to do.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pruned young. Explains the posture. And the attitude.

winter.intro: A winter pine. The cold kept you quiet on the outside while the roots drank everything. You think longer than you let on, and when you finally move, it's because you already decided weeks ago.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You look calm. Underneath, you've been planning since November.

gap-wood.strong:
Strong chart, Pine. Hand you a lanyard and you'd run the comeback, the group chat and the company.

Yeon: Comeback week, everyone's dead on their feet, and you're still sending voice notes about formation spacing at midnight.

Bom: You hold the room up when nobody else can. That part is real.

Yeon: You also fill the whole room. The quiet members got quieter and you didn't clock it.

Bom: Spend the extra on whoever is struggling with their part. Run it with them once, then step back.

Yeon: And leave them some decisions. Even the wrong ones.
gap-wood.weak:
Light chart, Pine. You lead by example, never by volume.

Bom: You read the room before the music starts. You know who's off before they do.

Yeon: Then you hand them your line. And your spot. And your sleep.

Bom: Your own part comes first this week. Then help.

Yeon: The back row is a position, Pine, not a personality.

Bom: Quiet leaders still lead. Say the title out loud.

with-fans.text:
Your fans don't scream for you. They feel safe with you, which is a stranger kind of love.

Bom: They'd cut a compilation of every collar you've fixed and every bag you've carried off the bus.

Yeon: They'd cut another of you saying "okay, everyone" at the top of every live. It's a sound now.

Bom: At fan signs you remember names. You ask about their exams. From last year.

Yeon: Every letter says "please rest". You read every one. You don't rest.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: They'd trend a hashtag begging you to take one day off. You'd thank them and go to practice.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your serious face during the cute challenge has its own reaction gif.

the-encore.text:
Last song. The one that matters.

Bom: You lead because you can't watch someone struggle and do nothing.

Yeon: Which is exactly why you're last in line for your own help.

Bom: In any group you're in, the team, the friends, the family, practise taking the help you hand out.

Yeon: Somebody keeps offering to carry your bag. Hand it over. It's a bag, Pine.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Receiving is a skill. Yours needs reps.

solo-concept.heading: Your solo concept, designed by Yeon
solo-concept.text: Concept name: "The one who stayed." Title track: mid-tempo, huge chorus, a key change you'd personally insist on. Lyrics about not leaving when leaving was easier. Styling: deep green, charcoal, long coats.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: My only note: the wind machine stays on for the whole video.

gap-wood.title: You found the bathroom on day one and gave everyone directions.
gap-wood.text:
First day as a trainee. Nobody knows anything. You've already learned everyone's name, the schedule and the fastest route to the convenience store.

Bom: You're a natural {pos_lower}.

Yeon: You're a natural {pos_lower} and a natural "let me just fix that for you".
gap-wood.end: Yeon: Your position is obvious. What you're secretly famous for in the fandom is not. Next page.

cliff.gap-wood: Yeon: You on stage, Pine: you're not the flashiest. You're | the one every camera finds when the song hits the last chorus.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: Solo era concept: anthem. Big, upright, a song people sing at graduations. You'd cry at your own showcase.
